summary: Wilde told Robert Ross in April 1900 that he had added Pietro Branca-d'Oro to his circle, describing him as dark and gloomy and saying he loved him very much.

sources.quote: Homer talks much - a little too much - of you. He slightly suspects you of treachery, and your immediate return seems to him problematical. Your allusion to his conduct on a postcard was mysterious. How was the 'revision' painful? I have added one Pietro Branca-d'Oro to the group. He is dark, and gloomy, and I love him very much. I send you a photograph I took on Palm Sunday at Palermo. Do send me some of yours, and love me always, and try to read this letter. It is a labour of a week to read it.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, [April 1900], Rome - quoted whole from the paragraph above the Pietro sentence to the signature, because the setting is part of the evidence. The 'HOMER' here is Omero, anglicised - the same young Roman already on this map, seen from a different letter and under an English name. The photograph was taken at Palermo on Palm Sunday, 8 April 1900. The letter ends by asking Ross to love him always.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The whole of the record for Branca-d'Oro, and Wilde saying he loved him.

manuscript.repository: William Andrews Clark Memorial Library, UCLA
